what_happened: Main reverted commit 02837e0, which stranded two verified docs jobs (9bw7 and fy1x). Their work was the records-history design doc, its accepted decision, and two CHANGELOG entries. Job 20261023-165947-e7bd was meant to carry that work onto a new base, but it could not, because a producer's working copy holds only one commit and cannot read the archive branch. The operator did the carry by hand. They copied the doc, the decision and the changelog entries from archive/next4-2026-10-23 onto a branch based on main, and renumbered decision D112 to D111. The text was otherwise unchanged.
cause: Athena treats a job as one producer run on a single-commit working copy, and it has no operation that moves verified work from one base to another. When the base moves, as with the revert, verified work on an archive branch is out of the producer's reach. The producer cannot read it, and the work is not reverified after the move. Renumbering decision IDs to fit the new base is a further mechanical step that nothing handles either. So the operator has to do the carry.
prevention: Add a code-level carry operation, for example `athena carry <job> --onto <base>`. It would take the verified jobs' diffs from their recorded commits or archive branch and apply them to a branch based on the target. It would renumber the decision IDs that collide, and it would run the repo's policy tests and a check that the content is unchanged apart from the renumbering. It would record the result as a landed job whose provenance points to the original verified jobs. The producer would never need to read another branch. The operation would also handle revert-stranded work in general.
proposed_request: Add a way for Athena to carry already-verified job work onto a new base without a producer reading another branch. Outcome: given one or more verified job IDs and a target base such as main, Athena produces a branch based on the target that has the same file changes as those jobs. It renumbers any decision IDs that collide with the target, and it keeps the CHANGELOG entries. It runs the repo's policy tests on the result. It records the carry, with provenance pointing to the original jobs, so it can be landed with `athena land`. Acceptance: (1) a test carries a verified docs job onto a base where its decision number is taken, and shows that the decision is renumbered, that nothing else in the text changes, and that references inside the carried text follow the new number; (2) a carry that conflicts with the target is refused with a clear message and leaves no partial branch; (3) the result passes the repo's tests and the history check. Then use it to carry the records-history design from jobs 9bw7 and fy1x from archive/next4-2026-10-23 onto main.
